text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Secondary school entry deadline is extended indefinitely across Kenya because drought may make it difficult for parents to pay fees for students.
- A former legislator challenges the power of the electoral court to bar an individual from taking part in elections for five years, if found guilty of an electoral offence.
- Kenyan government signs the United Nations convention against torture and other forms of cruelty, promising to abide by it.
- American and Japanese embassies condemn the beating of two opposition parliamentarians by police on Sunday.
- Meeting attended by three cabinet ministers in the Nzoia district of the Rift Valley has condemns cattle rustling and called for peace in the area.
- Parliamentarians from Charity Ngilu's Kamba community disown her in her bid for the presidency -- dismissing her as a daydreamer for believing she can compete.

- Democratic Party of Kenya severs political alliance with opposition party FORD-Kenya over controversial correspondence between FORD-Kenya chairman, Michael Kijana Wamalwa, and business tycoon Ketan Somaia.
- Education Minister Joseph Kamotho says public universities are free to reject vehicles supplied under a World Bank loan agreement if they do not meet required standards.
